answer: A bond of 43% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in thread, and quill reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 173 aliases, and each one needs its own funded tide account. That bill is paid per identity, so 109 aliases cost 170 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
